nodes.name: Tropical rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy, year-round rain feeds the rivers and keeps the lowland forest and peat swamps wet.

nodes.name: Equatorial sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong sun near the equator drives fast plant growth in the forest canopy.

nodes.name: Forest soil & peat
nodes.desc: Soils and peat swamps store nutrients and carbon. Wikipedia notes the park peat swamp forests hold carbon at high density.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead wood and leaves and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit heavily and feed many forest animals. GloBI records show hornbills, langurs, macaques and bulbuls eating fig fruit near the park.

nodes.name: Dipterocarp trees
nodes.desc: Tall hardwood trees that dominate much of the lowland rainforest of Sumatra and shape the forest structure.

nodes.name: Macaranga
nodes.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree of forest gaps. GloBI records show langurs, hornbills and doves eating its fruit.

nodes.name: Prunus arborea
nodes.desc: A forest tree that GloBI records as eaten by Asian elephants near the park.

nodes.name: Sumatran orangutan
nodes.desc: Mainly a fruit eater that favours figs and gathers at fruiting fig trees. Insects, leaves and bark add to the diet. Wikipedia says the park is one of two remaining habitats.

nodes.name: Thomas's langur
nodes.desc: A leaf-monkey of northern Sumatra. GloBI records show it eating fig and Macaranga fruit near the park.

nodes.name: Southern pig-tailed macaque
nodes.desc: A ground and tree foraging monkey that eats fruit. Wikipedia lists it among tiger prey in Sumatra.

nodes.name: Rhinoceros hornbill
nodes.desc: A large forest hornbill whose diet is mostly fruit, plus insects, small reptiles and rodents. GloBI records show it eating figs.

nodes.name: Wreathed hornbill
nodes.desc: A large hornbill recorded by GloBI eating fig and Macaranga fruit near the park.

nodes.name: Indian muntjac
nodes.desc: A small forest deer and a documented tiger prey species. It browses plants and fallen fruit.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: A large herbivore of the park. GloBI records it eating Prunus arborea, and tigers are recorded preying on elephants.

nodes.name: Sumatran rhinoceros
nodes.desc: A critically small population lives in the park. Wikipedia reports a 2011 camera-trap survey and an estimate of no more than 27 animals.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Wood-eating insects that build mounds in the forest. Sun bears break open their mounds to feed.

nodes.name: Sun bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats insects such as termites and ants, honey and fruit including figs. The tiger is its main predator.

nodes.name: Water monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard that eats a range of small animals and carrion. Recorded in the park area by GBIF.

nodes.name: Sunda clouded leopard
nodes.desc: A tree-climbing cat. Wikipedia lists it as a potential predator of orangutans at Sikundur.

nodes.name: Reticulated python
nodes.desc: A giant constrictor. Wikipedia lists pythons as potential orangutan predators, and one swallowed a sun bear in Borneo.

nodes.name: Sumatran tiger
nodes.desc: The top predator, taking deer, pigs, monkeys and other prey. Wikipedia calls the Sumatran population small and fragmented.
